manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: He tied one end to the last living trunk on his side, clipped the other end to his harness, swung the free end across the gap
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: A fixed end, clipped second end, and thrown free end cannot all refer to the two ends of one line.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: Specify which part is secured to which anchor/harness and who holds the actual free end in a continuous load path.

manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: They hurried back toward the bridge Arda had crossed.
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: Both protagonists are presented on the returning side; the text never establishes Nisa on the opposite bank before the rope is thrown to her.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: Declare Nisa's side before every rope throw, crossing, and bracing action. Show an actual route to an opposite ledge before she can catch an end.

manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: The bridge was dropping, and the line, still clipped to his harness and caught on the falling span, dragged him backward.
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: The bridge-line entanglement and direction of pull remain insufficiently defined for a reader to understand why cutting is necessary and safe.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: Map anchors, snag point, direction of force and Arda's footing; only then can a single deliberate cut release the falling-span load.

manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: He threw the coil across the gap. The wind bent it sideways, but on the second throw Nisa caught it.
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: The paid scene repair still does not establish Nisa's position on the far side; throwing the coil to her cannot fix an undefined crossing.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: Reject old repaired scene as a genuine quality ACCEPT; require an internally coherent shore-to-shore rescue path.

manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: She wrapped it around her forearm and hauled herself across hand over hand
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: Hauling hand-over-hand on a line fixed on the departure side only, without a documented far-side anchor or crossing procedure, does not establish safe suspension or progress.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: The crossing needs continuous support and a believable load-bearing anchor sequence; do not turn a rescue into a physically impossible tug.

manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: Arda unfastened the line from the trunk, coiled it with care
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: The gliders were briefly steadied by this line in exposed wind. They are subsequently left unattended; the text does not show a new reliable tie-down before returning.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: Verify how gliders remain secured to the root shore during the storm and whether the same route line is truly their sole way back.

manual_source_anchored_findings.quote: The corridor light, somewhere behind them, was dying.
manual_source_anchored_findings.finding: The explicit turnaround signal was triggered before the camp search, but the urgency is not consistently tracked through the journal discovery and return.
manual_source_anchored_findings.minimum_acceptance_obligation: Maintain the protagonists' emotional choice while preserving believable remaining flight time.
